title: Rubber bands on clarinets; giving an Albert to Handy
summary: They discuss clarinetists who held keys with rubber bands, and Thomas gave his last Albert to Handy while recalling John Lewis and Piku trying Boehm.

story.theme_name: The reed and horn player's craft: clarinet, sax, tone
story.community_name: Reeds, mouthpieces and horns: the reed player's gear

blocks.x: His clarinet did that have a lot of rubber bands on it?

No not that I know of. No. Did it? No. It didn't have a lot of rubber bands. Don's boy used to carry a lot of rubber bands. It was just Ernest Mowier. Oh yeah. Oh boy he died not long ago. Yeah. Well he used to have a lot of rubber bands on his clarinet. I really, every time he'd see it. Of course I used to carry some too myself. Sure that's very handy. I mean that's a good spring when your spring go bad. Yeah it sure is. I used to carry some rubber bands on mine too.

The reason why I said that I asked you that was I was talking to Kid Punch a few months ago. He always used to laugh at George your boy. He said why he had rubber bands on probably every key. I guess that must have been an old clarinet he had.

It might have been the one before that he gave me because I don't remember too many. There was a couple of them or so you know but as far as I can remember. But maybe that might have been one of the old ones you see. Yeah. Just when he bought another one.
Did you ever play that clarinet piece?

The one he had gave me? Yes it was the Albert system. I played it a good while. I mean I played it a long time. And so finally when I got to the band system. The last piece of Albert system clarinet I had I gave it to Handy. Because he said he tried to play a bam but he couldn't. So he had to do it with a little clarinet with Albert. So I had two pieces of it. Well I gave it to him. I couldn't find the rest of it. I gave it to Handy because I told him what the use of me having it. I don't think I'll be playing an Albert no more. Once I got on the bam I lost all face of trying to play the Albert. John Lewis had went to the bam once didn't he?

I don't remember that he ever told me that. I heard he didn't but I went back to the Albert. Piku told me once that he had learned a little bit on the bam but never did play it much I don't think. I think one time he could play both of them.
